title: Unregistered engine literals (LT1)
description: The rules of the census of unregistered literals in the engine paths (scripts/lib/literal_census.py, a module of scripts/structure-check): what counts as a value, what is not one, and which base tree bounds each count (D-068 (6), D-069 item 3).

literals.allowed_numbers.description: The numbers an engine file may spell outside the registry (the identity, the unit and the sign); every other number in a scanned file is an unregistered literal (LT1, D-069 item 3).

literals.allowed_values.description: The strings a pattern of literals.patterns finds that are not settings: the operating system's standard streams and its process file system (/proc, GATE-SPEED F4) and the portable interpreter lookup of a #! line. Every other match is an unregistered literal (LT1).

literals.base_ref.description: The ref whose merge-base with HEAD is the base tree when the census is given no --base: the allowed count of each unit, kind and value is the census of that tree, computed at check time and never stored (TX22, T2). A checkout without the ref fails closed.

literals.baseline.description: Deprecated (TX22): the list is no longer read; the allowed counts are the census of the base tree (literals.base_ref). Removed in a later revision (D-068 (3), expand then contract). Was: Directory of the engine's shrink-only list of unregistered literals (D-063 style, D-064 a): one <unit>.json per unit with the literals each file still spells, per kind and value. The census must equal it, and against the base no unit allows a value more times.

literals.patterns.description: Each kind of unregistered string literal, in order, and the regular expression that finds it inside a Python string or a shell or JavaScript line; a span one kind matched is not matched by the next. A host lists real top-level domains only, so the reserved test names of RFC 2606 (example.invalid, *.test) are not hosts. Numbers are judged by literals.allowed_numbers.

literals.unowned_area.description: The list area of a scanned file that no unit manifest owns (a fixture, or a checkout without manifests).
